newsitem.title: UK: Plummeting LME copper drags other metals down.
newsitem.headline: Plummeting LME copper drags other metals down.

text.p: Non-ferrous metal prices dived across the board on Thursday afternoon on the London Metal Exchange (LME) as a bear-raid on copper affected sentiment throughout the sector, traders said.

The flagship copper contract crashed though successive important chart support levels as investment fund liquidation triggered sell-stops and some panic selling. The other metals, previously immune to copper's gyrations, also tumbled.
"It's madness, copper is being sold off and everybody is looking to play it (the market) from the short side," one trader said.

Copper's volatility was highlighted by Thursday's range, with prices hitting an early morning peak of $2,037 a tonne before the rot set in. The three months price crashed to $1,935 before settling nervously around $1,950. On Wednesday prices ended around$2,020.

"What's happening is entirely down to technicals and options. The spreads have come right in, killing the backwardation and the delta business from options has been on the sell side," another trader said.

Recent volatility has been mainly due to the vagaries of the option market, with hedge cover driving the market up to 2-1/2 month highs at one point this week before positions were unwound, sending copper into a tailspin.

Traders said the current uncertainty in the market reflects a fundamental impasse, as physicals were quiet and the Chinese were sitting on the sidelines. Stock movements are neutral, but the contined contraction in the spreads signifies an easier trend in the last quarter of the year.
Other base metals came under pressure as well, with chart support levels giving way on aluminium, lead and nickel.
Aluminium, previously comfortable above $1,500, slipped to $1,486 at one stage against Wednesday's close of $1,508. Traders were nervous of declines towards $1,480 and below.
Nickel slumped under $7,500 to hit $7,420, a loss of $130 from yesterday, while lead ignored developing tightness in November and fell to $811, down some $4.50.
"At the moment it is all about copper. If that falls then there is not much to hold the others," a trader added.
